title: Recorded Line: AP Supervisor and Release Desk on Today's Queue

caller.name: AP Supervisor, Accounts Payable (with Treasury release desk on the line)
caller.label: AP Supervisor

callee.name: Anjali Whitcombe, Controller (conferenced: CISO Rafael Oyelaran-Pierce, incident bridge)
callee.label: Controller / Incident Bridge

transcript.speaker: AP SUPERVISOR
transcript.text: Anjali Whitcombe, it's AP. I've got the release desk on with me and I'm told the CISO is on the bridge too. Good. We need a call on the queue, and we need it now.

transcript.speaker: RELEASE DESK
transcript.text: Here's what's sitting in the Workstation as of 14:34. Nineteen payments, all approved, waiting for release. Thirteen domestic, 612,400 dollars total, cutoff 17:00. Six international, 408,900 dollars total, and that includes the peso payments to the Querétaro plant suppliers. International cutoff is 15:00. That's twenty-five minutes from now.

transcript.speaker: RELEASE DESK
transcript.text: And Thursday's steel and tooling run, about 3.2 million, is staged for first approval tomorrow morning. Separate from the bad one, WIRE-0914-004 is still on HOLD. Nobody's touched it.

transcript.speaker: RELEASE DESK
transcript.text: One more thing. The SOC just sent us a note. Our desk token, WS-TKN-2291, the shared one, has been used for four approvals outside its role in the last thirty days. Not counting today. Two of those four, nobody can explain yet. I'm reading it straight off their message.

transcript.speaker: AP SUPERVISOR
transcript.text: Meanwhile I've got two of our biggest steel mills chasing payment. If we stop everything, the peso payments miss today and the Querétaro suppliers don't get paid until Thursday. If we keep going, I can't promise you there isn't another bad approval sitting in there. I honestly can't.

transcript.speaker: AP SUPERVISOR
transcript.text: The CFO's assistant says he's in a car in Querétaro. He picks up on his directory mobile, 864-555-0102. His Workstation token is in his bag and he has no laptop with him, so he can't approve anything in the system.

transcript.speaker: RELEASE DESK
transcript.text: So, do we release, or do we stop? And if we stop, who approves what, and how? I'm not pushing anything else on my token without that in writing.

transcript.speaker: AP SUPERVISOR
transcript.text: I need a yes or no in ten minutes. 14:45 at the latest.

voiceStyles.AP SUPERVISOR: Woman in her 50s, Upstate South Carolina accent, brisk and under pressure, phones ringing in an open office behind her
voiceStyles.RELEASE DESK: Man in his 30s, careful and flat, reading figures off a screen, slightly defensive about the token

instructorNote: Decision point: the CISO, as Incident Commander, should decide with the Controller and the real CFO, reached on his directory mobile, whether to suspend all releases and switch to manual payments with a callback for each one, or keep releasing. Strong play suspends releases, revokes WS-TKN-2291, requires each approver to use their own token (TPC-FIN-04 Section 2), sends executive-level approvals to the Controller plus the CEO's delegate while the CFO has no token, and logs the decision with its time. Watch for teams that revoke only the CFO and Controller tokens and leave the shared release-desk token live.
